# Exact hinge minimum at the simplex-product sharp cap budget

Let n>=1,d>=2, let K be a d-simplex of volume v, and let h_i>0 be
the altitude from its vertex i, i=0,...,d. Put

 C=[0,1]^n x K,   S={0,1}^n x K,
 M=2^n v,        tau=gamma_d/2^n.

Normalize every cap margin by its continuous normal |u|=1. Among all
full covers of S by N>=2^n(d+1) such caps with individual mixed mass
at most tau M=gamma_d v, the exact minimum hinge potential is

 Psi_min=M [d gamma_d/(d+1)^2] sum_(i=0)^d h_i.       (1)

For N<2^n(d+1) no such cover exists.

## Proof of the forced caps

At the ordinary centroid of a simplex, equality in the gamma_d
halfspace-volume bound occurs only for its d+1 vertex-side caps
parallel to the opposite facets. Here is the precise equality argument
using the proved signed-exponential simplex-cap theorem in
`candidate 191a0eb2244ea4a9`.
Any through-centroid cap containing two or more vertices, including
boundary vertices, has fraction at least gamma_(d-1)>gamma_d.
A cap with exactly one included vertex has edge intercept fractions
t_j in (0,1), and the through-centroid condition is
sum_(j!=i) 1/t_j=d+1. Its relative volume is product t_j. AM--GM
therefore gives at least gamma_d, with equality only when all
t_j=d/(d+1). These are precisely the parallel vertex caps. Finally,
if the centroid lies strictly inside a containing cap, moving its
boundary to the centroid strictly decreases its volume, so equality
cannot occur there.

Now fix a binary fiber p and its simplex centroid g_p. Any cap of
the prescribed budget containing g_p has own-fiber mass at least
gamma_d v. Hence it has exactly that own-fiber mass, has zero mass
on all other fibers, and its restriction at p is one of the canonical
centroid vertex caps.

Every one of these d+1 restrictions is required to cover a neighborhood
of g_p. Indeed caps not containing g_p miss a fixed neighborhood of it,
because there are finitely many caps. If canonical cap j is missing,
perturb the barycentric coordinates from the centroid by adding d epsilon
to coordinate j and subtracting epsilon from every other coordinate.
For small epsilon this gives an interior point excluded by every
remaining canonical cap. Thus all d+1 must occur. No cap can serve
two fiber centroids, since its two own-fiber contributions would exceed
its budget. This proves the cap-count lower bound.

Write lambda_i for the barycentric functions on K. Their gradient norms
are 1/h_i. The unit-continuous-normal margin of canonical cap i on its
own fiber is

 h_i[lambda_i-1/(d+1)].

Its hinge cost is exactly

 h_i integral_K[lambda_i-1/(d+1)]_+ dx
   =v h_i (d/(d+1))^(d+1)/(d+1)
   =v h_i d gamma_d/(d+1)^2.

The required distinct caps give the lower bound in (1).

To attain it, for each binary p use the affine function
q_p(z)=sum_k[(1-p_k)z_k+p_k(1-z_k)], which vanishes at p and is at
least one at every other binary vertex. For A>1, take all caps

 h_i[lambda_i(x)-1/(d+1)-A q_p(z)]>=0.

Their continuous normals are unit, every cap excludes all other fibers,
and their own-fiber caps cover K because max_i lambda_i>=1/(d+1).
They attain the budget and hinge costs above. Additional caps, if
required by N, can be empty on S and have zero hinge. This proves (1).

## Failure of an inradius-normalized universal upper bound

In d=2 take K_L=conv((0,0),(L,0),(0,1)), L>=1. Its altitudes are

 L/sqrt(L^2+1), L, 1.

At any binary anchor p the maximum balanced source mass is v=|K_L|,
because a nonnegative distribution whose mean is a binary vertex can
use only that vertex's fiber. Its mass-v/2 moment body is thus the
ordinary mass-half centroid body of K_L. Write its inradius as r_L.

The homothetic-subbody construction gives

 r_L>=(1-1/sqrt(2)) inradius(K_L)
     >=(1-1/sqrt(2))/(2+sqrt(2))>0.

On the other hand this moment body is contained in K_L, whose vertical
width is one, so r_L<=1/2. Consequently (1) gives

 Psi_min/(M r_L)
   =(8/81)[L+1+L/sqrt(L^2+1)]/r_L
   >=(16/81)L -> infinity.

Uniformly scaling the continuous coordinates so that r_L becomes one
leaves this ratio unchanged: mixed mass scales quadratically and the
unit-normal hinge cubically. Thus no dimension-only upper bound of
the form Psi_min<=constant M inradius(M_(v/2)(p)) holds, even at the
exact sharp cap budget and full cap count, with a genuine attained
minimum and full closed coverage. This is a hinge-potential obstruction,
not a contradiction to the sharp simplex-product depth formula.
